title: #daystrom-telemetry-csv
subtitle: Every email about the Daystrom report / telemetry CSV, unspooled out of its threads and forwards and replayed as one continuous conversation. 55 messages + 3 meeting notices, 25 November 2025 → 20 August 2026. Hover any message for a # permalink, follow ↩ in reply to to jump to its parent, and the dotted underlines in the commentary link to the message being referenced. Searches, threads and avatar provenance are in the panels above.
openItems: What value Daystrom expects in the Berth Name column, and whether it lives in the Billing Agent Membership spreadsheet. Asked 20 Aug and unanswered — this is the column the report currently emits as PLACEHOLDER TBD, so it blocks the real file.
Who sends the member-facing invoices once the CSV is live — Starfleet directly, or Daystrom through their own system. Asked 20 Aug, unanswered.

Leah expects five members on the first billing file; Starfleet is sending one. He listed Vega Relay, Kepler's, Denobula Yard, Ferrix Dock and Lumen Direct on 19 Aug; Deanna replied the same morning that it will be a single client. Leah and Jo are holding member communications until this is settled.

Leah's two direct questions are unanswered — when the last payment members make direct to Starfleet will be, and whether the first Daystrom bill covers August consumption. Both are prerequisites for telling members anything.

Will was asked to call Leah on the morning of 19 Aug to name the single September client, and Deanna has already told Leah to expect it. That action currently sits with Will and nothing in email records it as done.

Which retailer the pilot uses. The client is now settled — Will confirmed Kepler Station to Leah on 20 Aug. Retailer is still open: the 18 Aug meeting settled on Vulcan Freight-only, at 17:16 that day Deanna proposed Utopia Planitia instead, and nothing since names one.
Daystrom has not answered how the file should be delivered. Jean-Luc asked Soong on 18 Aug; Will asked Leah again on 20 Aug. Asked twice, still unanswered.

Whether Daystrom's production deploy actually happened. Soong said on 9 Jul that e2e was complete and they were “good to go with the changes in Production next week”, gated on a business-team walkthrough of the member statement. Nothing since confirms it shipped, and Starfleet was never invited to the walkthrough.
Andorian Power's billing terms are still unknown, and are now the stated reason for restricting September to one client — Deanna says many sites sit with them and he needs time to align them.

The Registry Code → Fellow Number rename was queried on 17 Mar 2026 and never answered. Soong asked twice — “Is there a reason for this change? Can't we keep the same column as that of Vulcan Freight?” — against both renamed columns. The file must match Daystrom's template exactly or their system strips the data, so a renamed header is a live failure mode for the 2 September file.

Billing CSV export still to be updated to 2% + Duty commission, reported Inc-Duty, with bill_amount_fee recalculated to match — flagged 2 Aug as that week's first priority, and now due before a real customer's file goes out on 2 September.

Tasha's list of recently-switched sites never reached Leah. Her 19 Aug reply opens “Hi Leah” but was addressed only to Deanna, so Bajor Depot, Selar Outpost and Corvan Depot are unknown on the Daystrom side.
Registry code must move from the master sheet into the database — assigned at the 18 Aug meeting; no email confirms it done.
Late-payment reminders for Daystrom clients are still on. Jean-Luc to coordinate with Emil/Julie; Daystrom carries the collection risk, so duplicate chasing is a live customer-facing risk.

Utopia Planitia will not guarantee actual meter reads for Kepler Station (29 Jul) — the client asked for no estimated bills, and the last over-estimate produced large credits. Only a best-effort commitment was given. Kepler's is also on Leah's list for the first file.
Formal handover of billing-file generation initiated at the 17 Aug WarRoom; the 18 Aug meeting names Will for file generation, but no handover completion is recorded.
Daystrom entity hierarchy in the DB still inconsistent (the 14 misaligned sensor IDs), which feeds the same billing and reporting scope.

messages.body:
Thanks for jumping on a call this morning. It was really helpful to get a better understanding of your processes and requirements.

Firstly, Soong, below is a summary of the data format that we are planning to share with Daystrom. I've listed the columns that Vulcan Freight is currently providing, and the Columns that we intend to provide, plus a note about any changes between the two. If there are any changes you require then please let me know.

Original (Vulcan Freight)New (Starfleet)CommentSOONG (Daystrom)
Registry CodeFellow NumberChange of column name, representing the same dataIs there a reason for this change? Can't we keep the same column as that of Vulcan Freight?
NameAccount NameChange of column name, representing the same dataIs there a reason for this change? Can't we keep the same column as that of Vulcan Freight?
Statement DateStatement DateNo changeOK
Account NumberAccount NumberNo changeOK
Total Amt (Incl Duty)Total Amt (Incl Duty)No changeOK
Duty AmtDuty AmtNo changeOK
sensor IDsensor IDNo changeOK
CommissionCommissionNo changeOK
Amount (incl Duty) after CommissionAmount (incl Duty) after CommissionNo changeOK
TOU Energy ChargesDeleted; Starfleet will not include this columnOK
Last Billed Actual Read for this ConsumerDeleted; Starfleet will not include this columnOK
Estimate Read TypeRead Typeactual or estimatedOK (Is the column name being changed from Starfleet as compared to the Vulcan Freight?)
Berth NameAliasNo changeOK (Is the column name being changed from Starfleet as compared to the Vulcan Freight?)
sensor ID AddressSupply AddressNo changeOK (Is the column name being changed from Starfleet as compared to the Vulcan Freight?)
DiscountDiscountNo changeOK
Billing TypeDeleted; Starfleet will not include this columnOK

Additionally, below are the questions we discussed on call which would be great to confirm.

  • Registry Code: Confirming that this represents the membership number that each member has with Daystrom — Soong: Correct, this is the unique membership number that each Daystrom member has. Some examples are: R20486, 3684, 1010002051, M10732 and 0158
  • Name: Confirming that this represents an account name — Soong: Correct. This is the Account name that has been registered with Daystrom.
  • Discount: Confirming that this is the discount which the end customer incurs by using Daystrom for their energy — Soong: This is the Rebates that is printed on the member statement as it is when we receive from Vulcan Freight.
  • Amount (incl Duty) after Commission: Confirming that this is the amount that members must pay to Daystrom — Soong: No, This amount from this field “Amount (incl Duty) after Commission” is stored as extras in the invoice Database tables. This is not shown on the member statement.
  • Total Amt (Incl Duty): Confirming that this is the amount that Daystrom must pay to the energy retailer — Soong: No, this is the amount that members will pay to Daystrom. This is the same amount that will be present on the member's statement.

Finally, could you please share a copy of the following:

  • The consolidated statement that you send to customers — Soong: Attached is the member statement.
  • A copy of the PDF bill that Vulcan Freight sends to the end users — Soong: Attached is the same.
  • A copy of the onboarding form that you use to set up new accounts with Vulcan Freight — Soong: We don't have the Onboarding form. Vulcan Freight deals with this.

The origin of the entire trail, nine months before anything else here, and the closest thing to a written spec for the CSV. Soong's answers in the fourth column and after each dash were added later, on 17 March. Two things matter: the Registry Code → Fellow Number rename was queried and never answered — it is still an open action nine months on — and Soong corrected both money columns here in November 2025, Total Amt (Incl Duty) is what the member pays Daystrom, not what Daystrom pays the retailer. That is the exact point re-argued from scratch over 6–16 July 2026.

messages.body:
Yes, I can report back that the ingestion of the file was successful at our end.

  • We are now progressing with integration testing / e2e testing with our downstream systems.
  • At this stage, we are looking at 2 weeks from now for us to complete our e2e testing.
  • During this testing, we generate a Starfleet Invoice PDF form our internal systems.
  • This Starfleet PDF invoice contains all the information that's consumed from the source file such as the Account number, sensor ID details, Property etc. Let me know If you would like a sample of the PDF Invoice.
  • Post e2e testing, we would be able to generate a Daystrom member statement with the Starfleet PDF Invoice attached to it.
  • We would then provide the walkthrough of this member statement to the wider business team
  • Providing the Approval at the walkthrough meeting, we then deploy this change to our Prod systems.

This is the answer to the question the other thread asked on 18 May and never got. Daystrom ingested the test file successfully on 11 June — three weeks after Soong told Jean-Luc he was still “in the process of testing”, and it was reported to Geordi, not to Jean-Luc or Will. It also lays out Daystrom's full internal gate: e2e → member statement → business-team walkthrough → prod deploy. No tz stated in the quoted attribution, so none is shown.

What we can do is set these accounts up on summary billing. We can also provide a billing file alongside the summary invoice to assist with payment processing and reconciliation.

Summary invoices and billing files are generally issued after the 5th working day of each month, once the previous month's billing has been completed.

messages.body:
We wouldn't be able to generate and send out a summary invoice and file on the 1st of the month — the summary invoicing is done on the 4th or 5th working day of the month to allow time to ensure we have the metering data for all accounts.

What I was going to suggest is to set up a summary invoice for Keplers and Denobula Yard (separate summaries and billing files for each customer) to generate on the 5th working day of each month, but set the payment due date for all accounts to the 20th of the following month — i.e. an invoice sent on the 6th of August would not be due until the 20th of September. This would allow you to process the invoices for payment on or before the 1st, before they are due on the 20th.

If you require each account to be invoiced individually as they are now, we can still set the payment due dates to the 20th of the following month, but we wouldn't be able to send a billing file as such. We could, however, send a billing report each month. The difference is that the report does not include any open balances — so if a network discount was applied to the accounts, this would not show on the report but it would show in a summary invoice file.

The workaround the whole schedule now rests on: Utopia Planitia can't move when it invoices, only when payment falls due.

I've arranged for the accounts to be set up on summary invoicing going forward, and all accounts have been changed so that payment is due on the 20th of the following month.

Regarding the estimated bill request, I don't believe this is something we can accommodate. If a site has a legacy meter or a non-communicating smart meter where we attempt to manually read the meter every second month, all invoices for these sites are essentially estimated.

messages.label: Catch up in Daystrom billing — meeting held, 13:00 AEST · Deanna, Will, Jean-Luc
messages.body:
The 2 September rollout is postponed. Instead: a pilot with a single Vulcan Freight-only client — Rigel Station, pending verification that all its sites are Vulcan Freight — running one payment file for Vulcan Freight bills only, to validate the end-to-end process before a full rollout.

Why: the retailers' terms don't line up. Vulcan Freight aligns invoice dates to the payment-file deadline (invoices ~5 days after the 20th, leaving a 2–3 day buffer). Utopia Planitia keeps standard invoice dates of the 5th–7th, so its invoices arrive too late for that month's file — mitigated only because its 6-week terms let them ride into the next file. Andorian Power's terms are still unknown, and that is the open risk for a full rollout.

Hard constraint restated: the payment file must be sent by the 2nd of each month for payment on the 20th. Miss it and payment slips a full month. The file must match the existing template exactly — Daystrom's system strips data from modified cells.

Ownership split: Jean-Luc's team owns the technical process (file generation, data sync), Deanna owns the supplier relationships; Will owns file generation. The Registry code, currently in a master sheet, must be added to the database. Internal late-payment reminders are to be disabled for Daystrom clients, since Daystrom assumes the payment risk and collects directly.

Actions — Jean-Luc: verify Rigel Station is Vulcan Freight-only; introduce Will to Leah so Will owns pilot comms; email Daystrom IT to confirm the file submission method; sync Registry codes into the DB; coordinate with Emil/Julie on disabling reminders. Deanna: keep pursuing Andorian Power.

Two auto-recaps of the same 30 minutes: Gemini notes at 13:16 (msg 506c9e1982e05e9c) and the fuller Fathom recap Jean-Luc shared at 13:33 (msg 4d648e7a282c51d7). The detail above is Fathom's; Gemini's is a shorter paraphrase of the same decisions.

FYI

Nine minutes after the billing catch-up decided to postpone 2 September, Deanna forwards Leah's “are we still on track for the 2nd of September” across to engineering — without answering it.

Latest message in the trail. 09:20 AEST is 11:20 NZST, so it follows Deanna's 09:51 NZST message despite the earlier clock. Addressed “Hi Leah” but sent only to Deanna — Leah has not received this list, which means the member count for the first file is still open on both sides.

messages.subject: Starfleet x Daystrom Billing Pilot
messages.body:
Hi Leah, sorry for the delay.

I want to confirm that we will use Kepler Station as the individual client we will process as the pilot.

I still have a few outstanding questions.

  • Earlier in our communications we confirmed that Registry Code was the same as “Billing Agent Membership Number” column in this sheet. Is there a particular value your system expects in the Berth Name column, and is that contained in that same spreadsheet?
  • For the initial test we can send the full Kepler Station CSV over email, but following that what is your preferred way for us to communicate the CSV to you?
  • Once we are using the CSV, do you still want us to send out our Starfleet branded invoices directly to the members or will you handle those communications through your system?

Once these questions are resolved I can put together the CSV for all Kepler invoices.

I have attached another example CSV built from 2 real Kepler invoices from August, barring the above questions (and any feedback from your team) this will be the format that we provide.

Settles the pilot client, which had been unresolved since the 18 Aug Utopia Planitia-vs-Vulcan Freight exchange — but re-asks the delivery question Jean-Luc put to Soong on 18 Aug and never got an answer to, and raises Berth Name, the column the report currently emits as PLACEHOLDER TBD. No reply as at this build.
